Create, start, stop, pause, resume, fork, recover and delete isolates and microVMs.

## List sandboxes

`GET /v1/sandboxes` (SDK method `listSandboxes`)

The account's sandboxes the caller may see, newest first: by default the ones starting, running or stopping; `all` adds stopped, paused and errored ones. Deleted ones are left out. A key needs `sandboxes:read`.

**Query parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `account` | string | no | The account to act in: the caller's personal account (the default for a person) or an organisation they belong to. An API key always acts in its own account, and naming another is `forbidden`. |
| `state` | [SandboxState](/api/reference/types/#sandboxstate) | no | `starting`: being placed and booted. `running`: commands run now. `stopping`: its disk is being saved. `moving`: being moved to another host (`POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/move`; its `move` says how far), then started there; commands and file calls wait for it as they do for a start, except while a running sandbox's first copy is made (`copying`), when it still runs them. `stopped`: no machine; its disk is kept as its newest snapshot, and running programs are gone. `paused`: like `stopped`, but its memory is kept too, so `resume` carries on where it left off (microVMs only). `error`: the last operation failed or the machine was lost; `recover` or `resume` it. `deleting`, `deleted`: erased for good, with its snapshots. |
| `all` | boolean | no | Include stopped, paused and errored sandboxes. Default: only active ones. |
| `label` | Record&lt;string, string&gt; | no | Only those with each label: `label.ticket=PROJ-12`. |
| `host` | string | no | Only those on this host, a host's ID or name: one of the account's own hosts, or for a super-admin any host. |
| `mine` | boolean | no | Only the caller's own: the ones they made, in the console or with any of their API keys. |
| `limit` | integer | no | At most this many; default 50. (minimum 1, maximum 500) |
| `cursor` | string | no | A previous page's `nextCursor`. |

**Answers**

- `200`: [SandboxPage](/api/reference/types/#sandboxpage) (`application/json`). A page of sandboxes.

**Errors**: `400` invalid, `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` not_found. Each is an [ErrorBody](/api/reference/types/#errorbody).

## Create a sandbox

`POST /v1/sandboxes` (SDK method `createSandbox`)

Makes a sandbox and starts it: an isolate unless `type` says `microvm`, from a snapshot when `from` names one. `resources` sets its vCPUs and memory, and a microVM's disk (`diskGb`), which may also go alone or beside `size` (`getSandboxShapes` says what may be asked); `size`, a named size, still works for now. Answers as soon as it is placed (`starting`), or once it runs with `wait`. A full deployment is `exhausted`; no host able to run the type is `unavailable`. `mounts` (experimental) are for microVMs only: an isolate's are refused (`not_supported`), because an isolate is a shell over files the host keeps, with no file system of its own to mount a drive or a bucket into. A mount whose bundle or bucket source isn't the account's is `not_found`; with the deployment's `KANTEL_MOUNTS` switch off, any `mounts` are `not_supported`. A key needs `sandboxes:write`.

**Header parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Idempotency-Key` | string | no | A key of your choosing, unique per call, such as a UUID. A retry with the same key gets the first call's answer and does nothing again. While the first call is still working, a retry is `conflict` (`details.idempotencyKey` `in_progress`): retry it later. A first call that didn't finish (it failed part way, or stopped answering) is never done again under its key: a retry is `conflict` (`held`), so check, then use a new key. The same key with a different request is `refused`. (at most 255 characters) |

**Body**: [CreateSandboxBody](/api/reference/types/#createsandboxbody)

**Answers**

- `201`: [Sandbox](/api/reference/types/#sandbox) (`application/json`). The sandbox.

**Errors**: `400` invalid, `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` not_found, `409` conflict, `422` refused, `429` exhausted, `501` not_supported, `503` unavailable. Each is an [ErrorBody](/api/reference/types/#errorbody).

## Get the shapes a sandbox may be

`GET /v1/sandbox-shapes` (SDK method `getSandboxShapes`)

What a new sandbox in the account may be, from the hosts it may use: an isolate's memory, a microVM's vCPUs and memory, the hosts' presets and what an hour costs. With `host`, from that host alone. A key needs `sandboxes:read`.

**Query parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `account` | string | no | The account to act in: the caller's personal account (the default for a person) or an organisation they belong to. An API key always acts in its own account, and naming another is `forbidden`. |
| `host` | string | no | The shapes a sandbox pinned to this host (`CreateSandboxBody.host`, its ID or name) may be, from that host alone. Default: from every host the account's sandboxes may use. |
| `pool` | string | no | The shapes a sandbox in this pool (`CreateSandboxBody.pool`, its ID or name) may be, from its hosts. Default: from the hosts a create naming no pool may use, in the default pools. |

**Answers**

- `200`: [SandboxShapes](/api/reference/types/#sandboxshapes) (`application/json`). The shapes.

**Errors**: `400` invalid, `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` not_found. Each is an [ErrorBody](/api/reference/types/#errorbody).

## Start a sandbox

`POST /v1/sandboxes/{sandboxId}/start` (SDK method `startSandbox`)

Boots a stopped, paused or errored sandbox fresh from its newest disk snapshot: programs start again, and a paused sandbox's memory is let go. To carry on where a paused sandbox left off, `resume` it instead. A running sandbox is answered as it is. A key needs `sandboxes:write`.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sandboxId` | string | yes | The sandbox's ID. |

**Body**: [ResumeSandboxBody](/api/reference/types/#resumesandboxbody)

**Answers**

- `200`: [Sandbox](/api/reference/types/#sandbox) (`application/json`). The sandbox, starting.

**Errors**: `400` invalid, `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` not_found, `409` conflict, `429` exhausted, `501` not_supported, `503` unavailable. Each is an [ErrorBody](/api/reference/types/#errorbody).

## Stop or pause a sandbox

`POST /v1/sandboxes/{sandboxId}/stop` (SDK method `stopSandbox`)

Saves its disk as a snapshot and lets the machine go; running programs end. With `keepMemory`, pauses it instead, keeping its memory too (microVMs only; `not_supported` on an isolate). A stopped sandbox costs nothing to run. A key needs `sandboxes:write`.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sandboxId` | string | yes | The sandbox's ID. |

**Body**: [StopSandboxBody](/api/reference/types/#stopsandboxbody)

**Answers**

- `200`: [Sandbox](/api/reference/types/#sandbox) (`application/json`). The sandbox, stopping.

**Errors**: `400` invalid, `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` not_found, `409` conflict, `501` not_supported, `503` unavailable. Each is an [ErrorBody](/api/reference/types/#errorbody).

## Resume a sandbox

`POST /v1/sandboxes/{sandboxId}/resume` (SDK method `resumeSandbox`)

Carries on a paused sandbox from its memory, or starts a stopped one from its newest snapshot, on the same size or the one given. Same ID; a new machine. A key needs `sandboxes:write`.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sandboxId` | string | yes | The sandbox's ID. |

**Body**: [ResumeSandboxBody](/api/reference/types/#resumesandboxbody)

**Answers**

- `200`: [Sandbox](/api/reference/types/#sandbox) (`application/json`). The sandbox, starting.

**Errors**: `400` invalid, `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` not_found, `409` conflict, `429` exhausted, `501` not_supported, `503` unavailable. Each is an [ErrorBody](/api/reference/types/#errorbody).

## Fork a sandbox

`POST /v1/sandboxes/{sandboxId}/fork` (SDK method `forkSandbox`)

Makes `count` new sandboxes, each a copy of this one's newest snapshot (or `snapshotId`); a running microVM on a host that can fork live is copied with its memory. The source doesn't change. A microVM fork is its source's machine (its `resources` from the start) unless `size` names another, and gets the source's exposed ports, each public or gated as it was, at its own URLs once it runs (only for a caller with `access`, as they are exposed as the caller). A key needs `sandboxes:write`.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sandboxId` | string | yes | The sandbox's ID. |

**Header parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Idempotency-Key` | string | no | A key of your choosing, unique per call, such as a UUID. A retry with the same key gets the first call's answer and does nothing again. While the first call is still working, a retry is `conflict` (`details.idempotencyKey` `in_progress`): retry it later. A first call that didn't finish (it failed part way, or stopped answering) is never done again under its key: a retry is `conflict` (`held`), so check, then use a new key. The same key with a different request is `refused`. (at most 255 characters) |

**Body**: [ForkSandboxBody](/api/reference/types/#forksandboxbody)

**Answers**

- `201`: [ForkedSandboxes](/api/reference/types/#forkedsandboxes) (`application/json`). The new sandboxes.

**Errors**: `400` invalid, `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` not_found, `409` conflict, `422` refused, `429` exhausted, `501` not_supported, `503` unavailable. Each is an [ErrorBody](/api/reference/types/#errorbody).

## Upgrade an isolate to a microVM

`POST /v1/sandboxes/{sandboxId}/upgrade` (SDK method `upgradeSandbox`)

Turns a running or stopped isolate into a microVM with the same ID, name, labels, env, environments, egress grants and protected variables. Its `/workspace` files are put in the microVM at `/home/user/workspace`, and `/workspace` there is a link to them, so paths an agent used keep working. A stopped isolate comes back as a running microVM. Upgrade when a command answers `needsMicrovm`, or before work an isolate can't do (`git`, Node or Python packages, a build, Docker). Answers once the microVM runs (unless `wait` is `false`), and a microVM is answered as it is. If the microVM can't be made, the call fails and the isolate is left as it was. Commands and file calls made meanwhile wait for it. Its isolate time ends and its microVM time starts at the upgrade; a `sandbox.upgraded` event records it. A key needs `sandboxes:write`.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sandboxId` | string | yes | The sandbox's ID. |

**Header parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Idempotency-Key` | string | no | A key of your choosing, unique per call, such as a UUID. A retry with the same key gets the first call's answer and does nothing again. While the first call is still working, a retry is `conflict` (`details.idempotencyKey` `in_progress`): retry it later. A first call that didn't finish (it failed part way, or stopped answering) is never done again under its key: a retry is `conflict` (`held`), so check, then use a new key. The same key with a different request is `refused`. (at most 255 characters) |

**Body**: [UpgradeSandboxBody](/api/reference/types/#upgradesandboxbody)

**Answers**

- `200`: [Sandbox](/api/reference/types/#sandbox) (`application/json`). The sandbox, now a microVM.

**Errors**: `400` invalid, `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` not_found, `409` conflict, `422` refused, `429` exhausted, `501` not_supported, `503` unavailable. Each is an [ErrorBody](/api/reference/types/#errorbody).

## Move a sandbox to another host

`POST /v1/sandboxes/{sandboxId}/move` (SDK method `moveSandbox`)

Moves a microVM to another host in its pool, with the same ID, name, settings and URLs: its disk and its sticky disks' copies (their uncommitted writes too) are copied to that host, it is started there, and only then is it placed there and its copy on the old host deleted. It never leaves its pool. Memory doesn't move yet: a paused or running sandbox is refused unless `keepMemory` is `false`, and then boots on its disk. A running one moves with a restart: it is copied as it runs, then stopped (its processes end), what it wrote since is copied, and it is started on the new host, so it is unavailable for seconds rather than for the whole copy. `hostId` picks the host; else the scheduler does, among the pool's hosts that can take it. While it moves its `state` is `moving`, and `move` says how far. Answers once it runs on the new host (unless `wait` is `false`). If it can't be moved, the call fails and it is left where it was: a running sandbox that was stopped for the move is started there again. Its automatic snapshots from before stay on the old host. A key needs `sandboxes:write`.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sandboxId` | string | yes | The sandbox's ID. |

**Header parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Idempotency-Key` | string | no | A key of your choosing, unique per call, such as a UUID. A retry with the same key gets the first call's answer and does nothing again. While the first call is still working, a retry is `conflict` (`details.idempotencyKey` `in_progress`): retry it later. A first call that didn't finish (it failed part way, or stopped answering) is never done again under its key: a retry is `conflict` (`held`), so check, then use a new key. The same key with a different request is `refused`. (at most 255 characters) |

**Body**: [MoveSandboxBody](/api/reference/types/#movesandboxbody)

**Answers**

- `200`: [Sandbox](/api/reference/types/#sandbox) (`application/json`). The sandbox, running on its new host (or `moving`).

**Errors**: `400` invalid, `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` not_found, `409` conflict, `422` refused, `429` exhausted, `501` not_supported, `503` unavailable. Each is an [ErrorBody](/api/reference/types/#errorbody).

## Restart a sandbox on the latest base

`POST /v1/sandboxes/{sandboxId}/restart-on-latest` (SDK method `restartSandboxOnLatest`)

Restarts the machine on the newest base image, on its disk as it is: a running sandbox's disk is saved and it is stopped first (as `stop` does, without its memory), then it boots cold on the latest base. Memory is lost, and so are running programs. A running sandbox is never patched underneath: this is how an outdated one (`base.outdated`) moves on. Answers once it is starting. A sandbox starting, stopping or being deleted is `conflict`; one another call moves after this restart has stopped it is `aborted`. A key needs `sandboxes:write`. Experimental: `not_supported` unless the deployment has turned image patching on (`KANTEL_IMAGE_PATCHING`).

**Path parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sandboxId` | string | yes | The sandbox's ID. |

**Header parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Idempotency-Key` | string | no | A key of your choosing, unique per call, such as a UUID. A retry with the same key gets the first call's answer and does nothing again. While the first call is still working, a retry is `conflict` (`details.idempotencyKey` `in_progress`): retry it later. A first call that didn't finish (it failed part way, or stopped answering) is never done again under its key: a retry is `conflict` (`held`), so check, then use a new key. The same key with a different request is `refused`. (at most 255 characters) |

**Answers**

- `200`: [Sandbox](/api/reference/types/#sandbox) (`application/json`). The sandbox, starting.

**Errors**: `400` invalid, `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` not_found, `409` conflict, `422` refused, `429` exhausted, `501` not_supported, `503` unavailable. Each is an [ErrorBody](/api/reference/types/#errorbody).

## Get a sandbox's usage

`GET /v1/sandboxes/{sandboxId}/usage` (SDK method `getSandboxUsage`)

CPU, memory, running time and cost per interval, and in `series` its readings as they came (every 5 seconds over the last hour from a current host). Poll with `since` set to the last series point's `at` for only the newer points. A key needs `sandboxes:read`.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sandboxId` | string | yes | The sandbox's ID. |

**Query parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `since` | integer | no | From this time; default 24 hours ago. `series` then holds only the points after it, so a client polls with the last point's `at`. |
| `intervalSeconds` | integer | no | Default 300. (minimum 60, maximum 86400) |

**Answers**

- `200`: [SandboxUsage](/api/reference/types/#sandboxusage) (`application/json`). The usage.

**Errors**: `400` invalid, `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` not_found. Each is an [ErrorBody](/api/reference/types/#errorbody).

## List a sandbox's busiest processes

`GET /v1/sandboxes/{sandboxId}/processes` (SDK method `listSandboxProcesses`)

A running microVM's busiest processes, as `top` would list them: each one's CPU over a short sample (about half a second, read when asked) and resident memory, by CPU, then memory. Read from the sandbox's guest agent and kept nowhere. A sandbox that isn't running is `conflict`. An isolate, which shares its runtime with the account's other isolates, is `not_supported`, as is a sandbox whose host or guest agent is from before they could be listed. Command lines are what the sandbox runs, arguments and all, so this needs the scope that running `ps` would. A key needs `exec`.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sandboxId` | string | yes | The sandbox's ID. |

**Query parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | integer | no | How many to list: default 10, at most 50. (minimum 1, maximum 50) |

**Answers**

- `200`: [SandboxProcessList](/api/reference/types/#sandboxprocesslist) (`application/json`). Its busiest processes.

**Errors**: `400` invalid, `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` not_found, `409` conflict, `501` not_supported, `503` unavailable. Each is an [ErrorBody](/api/reference/types/#errorbody).
